papers.title: Two-dimensional magnetic interactions in LaFeAsO
papers.abstract: Inelastic neutron scattering measurements demonstrate that the magnetic interactions in antiferromagnetic LaFeAsO are two-dimensional. Spin wave velocities within the Fe layer and the magnitude of the spin gap are similar to the \textit{A}Fe$_2$As$_2$ based materials. However, the ratio of interlayer and intralayer exchange is found to be less than $\sim 10^{-4}$ in LaFeAsO, very similar to the cuprates, and $\sim$ 100 times smaller than that found in \textit{A}Fe$_2$As$_2$ compounds. papers.title: Supersymmetry anomalies in new minimal supergravity
papers.abstract: We determine the general structure of quantum anomalies for the $R$-multiplet of four dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric quantum field theories in the presence of background fields for an arbitrary number of Abelian flavor multiplets. candidate_claims.description: Inelastic neutron scattering study of LaFeAsO demonstrating anomalously 2D magnetic interactions (Jc/J+ < 10⁻⁴, similar to cuprates) despite moderate Fe-layer spacing (~8.7 Å), in stark contrast to AFe2As2 compounds (Jc/J+ ≈ 2–6%). Spin gap (~11.6 meV) and in-plane spin velocities resemble 122 materials, but interlayer exchange is ~100× weaker—an anomaly showing magnetic dimensionality varies dramatically across iron arsenide families, with potential implications for maximum superconducting Tc.
